findings.title: prices/history.json frozen at 2026-05-17 — backtest stack starved of forward prices
findings.description: Global max date across all 17177 tickers in prices/history.json is 2026-05-17, but today is 2026-06-13 and picks-history vintages run through 2026-06-12. Every vintage dated after ~2026-05-17 has no exit price within the 28d/84d horizon, so pickReturn/universeMedian/benchmark all resolve to null. The walk-forward and method-effectiveness reports therefore reflect at most ~4 vintages of real data (05-08..05-17), the rest silently contribute nothing while the maturity gate marks them 'too-early' or yields null alpha.
findings.mechanism: nearestTradingDay/_priceAtCanonical scan only +-5/-7 days from the target date; when the price series ends 05-17, any target beyond 05-22 returns null -> returnPct null -> dropped from cohort. No error is raised; vintageCount and totalPicks shrink invisibly.
findings.reproducer: node -e "const h=require('./prices/history.json');let m='0';for(const t in h){const s=h[t];if(Array.isArray(s)&&s.length){const d=s[s.length-1].date;if(d>m)m=d}}console.log(m)"  ->  2026-05-17
findings.impact: All alpha/effectiveness numbers in outputs/ are computed from a tiny, stale slice of vintages. Decisions to keep/retire methods (methodology-report) rest on near-zero forward-price coverage. Any positive alpha shown is from <=4 overlapping early-May vintages.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a freshness assertion at the top of walk-forward-perf.js / method-effectiveness.js: if max(price date) < today-3 business days, log ::error:: and skip (or fail CI). Root-cause why pull-historical-prices stopped updating after 05-17.

findings.title: Benchmark series SPY/QQQ/IWM nearly empty (SPY=3 points) — alphaVsBenchmark unusable
findings.description: In the live prices/history.json, SPY has 3 data points (2026-05-14..2026-05-17), IWM 3, QQQ 8 (2026-05-08..2026-05-17). computeBenchmarkReturn picks the first present ticker (SPY) and anchors ALL per-vintage canonical entry/exit dates to it. With a 3-point SPY series, the benchmark return is null for every vintage whose entry is outside 05-14..05-17, and the canonical-date anchoring then forces pick/universe/frozen-vintage lookups onto those same unavailable dates.
findings.mechanism: computeBenchmarkReturn returns {entryDate,exitDate} from SPY's sparse map; evaluateVintage threads that pair into _priceAtCanonical for every pick. If SPY can't resolve the window, canonical is still built from whatever SPY snapped to (or null), starving the whole vintage's measurement.
findings.impact: alphaVsBenchmark / medianAlphaVsBenchmark (the metric methodology-report labels 'most honest') is null or computed from a 3-day SPY window. The benchmark column in every report is effectively noise.
findings.suggested_fix: Backfill full SPY/QQQ/IWM history (>=120d) in pull-historical-prices; assert benchmark series length >= horizon+buffer before anchoring canonical dates, else fall back to per-ticker windows and flag.

findings.title: backtest-from-history.js ignores HORIZON_DAYS — measures full available history span
findings.description: HORIZON_DAYS (default 70) is parsed from argv and written into the output JSON, but the return is computed as (series[last].close - series[0].close)/series[0].close — the entire price series, not a 70-day window. AAPL's series spans 2026-01-27..2026-05-17 (79 points), so the '70-day backtest' actually measures ~110 calendar days. Different tickers have different series lengths, so each stock's return is over a different, uncontrolled window.
findings.mechanism: startQ=series[0], endQ=series[series.length-1]. No date arithmetic against HORIZON_DAYS. The labeled horizon and the measured horizon are unrelated.
findings.reproducer: Read lines 27-31; series[0]..series[length-1] regardless of HORIZON_DAYS. Confirm AAPL series len=79 spanning Jan-May while horizon=70d.
findings.impact: Pass/fail cohort alpha is computed over heterogeneous windows mislabeled as a fixed 70-day horizon. Cross-stock comparison is invalid; the headline alpha is meaningless. Compounds with the look-ahead bias the script already self-flags (methods evaluated on TODAY's snapshot).
findings.suggested_fix: Snap start to the series entry nearest (endDate - HORIZON_DAYS) and end to the latest entry, using the same nearestTradingDay logic as walk-forward; or delete this script in favor of walk-forward-perf.js (already named as preferredAlternative).

findings.title: Vintage-count gate applied only to alphaVsUniverse; benchmark/frozen alpha ungated
findings.description: MIN_VINTAGES_UNIVERSE (4) gates only medianAlphaVsUniverse (and the medianAlpha alias). medianAlphaVsBenchmark, medianAlphaVsSpy, and medianAlphaVsFrozenVintage are reported as the raw median over however many vintages contributed — which, given F-BT-001/002, can be 1-2. methodology-report.js then surfaces medianAlphaVsBenchmark as the primary 'alpha vs Benchmark' column with no minimum-vintage guard.
findings.mechanism: medianAlphaVsUniverseGated checks universeAlphaVintageCount < 4; the sibling medianAlphaVsBenchmark/FrozenVintage lines call median(collect(...)) directly with no count gate.
findings.reproducer: Read lines 564-581: only the Universe branch has the MIN_VINTAGES_UNIVERSE gate; Benchmark/FrozenVintage have none.
findings.impact: Reports can show a confident-looking benchmark alpha derived from a single vintage's overlapping picks. Readers treat it as a stable estimate. Inconsistent gating across the three benchmarks is misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same MIN_VINTAGES gate (counting non-null contributing vintages) to medianAlphaVsBenchmark and medianAlphaVsFrozenVintage; emit a *Note field when gated.

findings.title: Pseudo-replication: overlapping daily vintages pooled as i.i.d. inflates significance
findings.description: Vintages are emitted almost daily (29 files in ~5 weeks). A 28d or 84d forward return for vintage D overlaps ~27/83 days with vintage D+1, and the same ticker recurs in consecutive vintages. bootstrapAlphaCI resamples pass/fail arrays treating every (vintage,ticker,return) row as an independent draw, and MIN_VINTAGES counts calendar dates not independent windows. Overlapping windows + repeated tickers violate independence, shrinking CIs toward false significance.
findings.mechanism: perMethod bucket.pass/fail accumulate one entry per (vintage,ticker); the bootstrap draws with replacement from these correlated rows. No block-bootstrap, no de-overlapping, no clustering by ticker.
findings.reproducer: ls picks-history | wc -l (29 daily vintages in 5 weeks); 28d horizon overlaps ~96% between consecutive vintages.
findings.impact: ciLo95>0 'significant' verdicts in method-effectiveness / methodology-report are anti-conservative. Methods may be promoted/retired on spurious significance.
findings.suggested_fix: Use non-overlapping vintages per horizon (sample every Nd), or a block/cluster bootstrap that resamples whole vintages (and de-duplicates tickers within a vintage). Report effective sample size.

findings.title: Multiple-comparison: ~30 methods x 2 horizons x 4 quality grades, no FWER/FDR control
findings.description: _evalGroup computes a 95% bootstrap CI per (method, horizon) and again per (method, horizon, quality grade A/B/C/D). With ~30 methods x 2 horizons x up to 5 groupings that is ~300 simultaneous CI tests, each at nominal 5% alpha. methodology-report flags any method with ciLo95>0 as 'significant — earns its score weight' and ciHi95<0 as 'retire'. With no Bonferroni/Benjamini-Hochberg correction, ~15 methods will appear significant by chance alone.
findings.mechanism: Independent per-cell 95% CIs, no correction; downstream report treats each crossing of zero as an actionable signal.
findings.reproducer: Count methods x horizons x grades emitted in method-effectiveness.json; each gets an independent 95% CI consumed as a decision.
findings.impact: Score-aggregator weight changes and method retirements driven by false positives. The quality-split table is especially exposed (smallest n, most tests).
findings.suggested_fix: Apply BH-FDR or Bonferroni across the full grid of CIs before labeling significance; require persistence across consecutive reports (the report already suggests 3 consecutive months for retirement — apply the symmetric bar for promotion).

findings.title: DST window in getEntryDate misclassifies early-March/late-Nov as EDT -> same-day look-ahead
findings.description: isEDT is approximated as month>=3 && month<=11. US DST actually runs 2nd-Sunday-March..1st-Sunday-November. For ~10 days in early March and ~25 days in November the market is on EST (close 21:00 UTC) but the code uses the EDT threshold (20:00 UTC). A snapshot at 20:00-21:00 UTC on those dates is pre-close but classified post-close, so no T+1 entry shift happens and the screener books the same-day close it could not have transacted at.
findings.mechanism: marketCloseUTC = isEDT ? 20 : 21; for a 20:30Z snapshot on 2026-03-01 the code returns same-day (verified) although EST close is 21:00.
findings.reproducer: node -e "console.log(require('./scripts/walk-forward-perf.js').getEntryDate('2026-03-01T20:30:00.000Z'))" -> 2026-03-01 (should shift to next day under EST).
findings.impact: Up to ~35 calendar days/year of vintages can include an intraday move the screener could not capture, mildly inflating measured returns for affected vintages. Low magnitude but a genuine look-ahead leak.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the actual DST transition (2nd Sun Mar / 1st Sun Nov) or just always use the conservative 21:00 UTC threshold (only over-shifts EDT post-20:00, which is safe/conservative).

findings.title: horizonActualDays exposed but never used — summary still pools 79-84d windows
findings.description: Tag 232c-27 added horizonActualDays 'so cross-vintage alpha aggregation can normalize windows' and it is now stored per-vintage (line 456). But the summary aggregation (collect/median over alphaVsSpy etc., lines 544-590) never reads horizonActualDays. Pre-holiday vintages whose exit backward-snaps to 79-82 days are pooled un-normalized with full 84d windows. The observability half shipped; the correction half did not.
findings.mechanism: median(collect('alphaVsSpy')) ignores the per-vintage window length; backward-first snapping (nearestTradingDay) systematically shortens exits across US holidays.
findings.reproducer: grep horizonActualDays scripts/walk-forward-perf.js — written at lines 306/456, read by nothing in the aggregation.
findings.impact: 84d-horizon aggregate alpha carries ~1pp window-length noise for volatile modes; the noise is one-sided (windows only shorten via backward snap), so it biases rather than merely adds variance.
findings.suggested_fix: Rescale per-vintage return by horizonNominalDays/horizonActualDays before aggregating, or drop vintages with |actual-nominal|>3d from the summary.

findings.title: Entry backward-snap books untradable weekend/holiday gap for Fri & pre-holiday vintages
findings.description: nearestTradingDay scans backward first to avoid look-ahead, and computeBenchmarkReturn uses it for the ENTRY date. For a vintage whose entryDate (already T+1 from getEntryDate) lands on a Saturday/Sunday/holiday, the entry snaps backward to the prior Friday close. The trade is then booked at a price from a day BEFORE the intended entry, capturing the over-weekend gap the screener could not have transacted (it 'decided' after Friday close). Backward-first fixes exit look-ahead but introduces a small entry-side gap-capture.
findings.mechanism: entryDate = nearestTradingDay(asOfDate, map); for a weekend target it returns Friday, and map.get(Friday) is used as p0, so the Fri->Mon gap is included in the pick return.
findings.reproducer: A vintage with getEntryDate landing on Sunday snaps entry to Friday; p0 = Friday close, capturing Fri-close..exit including the weekend gap the trader could not enter at.
findings.impact: Per-vintage entry-price bias of one weekend/holiday gap; sign depends on the gap. Affects a meaningful fraction of vintages given near-daily cadence. Note many live vintages have midnight-UTC asOf which getEntryDate shifts to T+1, increasing weekend-landing frequency.
findings.suggested_fix: For the ENTRY date snap forward to the next available trading day (the first day the trade could actually be placed) while keeping EXIT backward-snap; document the asymmetry.

findings.title: Survivor bias: early vintages have evaluatedTickers=0 and live universe swings 3300-5657
findings.description: evaluatedTickers is the only survivor-bias correction (universe median restricted to tickers actually in the universe at vintage time). The first 5 live vintages (2026-05-08..05-13) have evaluatedTickers length 0, so alphaVsUniverse is suppressed (correct), but those are exactly the only vintages with mature forward prices under F-BT-001. After 05-14 the count swings 5657->4147->3790->3339->...->3314->5056, a 50% week-to-week universe-size change. The universe-median benchmark is computed over wildly different populations across vintages, and delisted/removed tickers within a vintage still vanish from prices/history.json (no delisting prices retained), so even the corrected universe over-weights survivors.
findings.mechanism: evaluatedTickers comes from today's snapshot directory contents at snapshot time; it captures universe membership but not delisting outcomes. prices/history.json only contains tickers still pulled today, so a name dropped between vintage and maturity has no exit price and silently leaves the cohort.
findings.reproducer: node script iterating picks-history shows evalTk 0,0,0,0,0,5657,4147,3790,3339,... — unstable and zero for the early vintages.
findings.impact: Universe-median alpha is computed against an unstable, survivor-tilted reference. Cross-vintage comparability of alphaVsUniverse is undermined; magnitude of bias is unquantified.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist delisted-ticker final prices (last traded) so dropped names contribute their realized (often negative) return; alternatively report universe-size per vintage alongside alpha and gate when it deviates >X% from the median universe size.

findings.title: score-scale fallback: early vintages lack score; pick.score mixes 0-100 and absent
findings.description: pickStockForMode falls back from ev.score (0-100) to ev.normScore*100 to null. In the live corpus the first 5 vintages (05-08..05-13 for HYPERGROWTH) have no score at all (hyperScore=false), and picks are sorted/deduped by score with null-handling. dedupePicksByCompany breaks ties by (p.score||0): when score is null for a whole vintage every pick has effective score 0, so company-dedup keeps an arbitrary (first-inserted) duplicate rather than the better name, and the top-100 truncation order is driven by primaryMetric fallback only. This makes the actual pick SET differ in composition between scored and unscored vintages for reasons unrelated to the strategy.
findings.mechanism: picks.sort uses score when both non-null else primaryMetric; dedupe tie-break uses (p.score||0). With all-null score the sort collapses to primaryMetric and the dedupe tie-break collapses to insertion order.
findings.reproducer: node survey shows hyperScore=false for 2026-05-08..05-11; sample pick from 05-08 has no 'score' key.
findings.impact: Pick membership for early vintages is determined differently (metric-only) than later vintages (score-driven), confounding any cross-vintage performance comparison and the dedupe outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Backfill score for legacy vintages or tag them with a scoreSource field; have walk-forward/method-effectiveness exclude or separately bucket vintages with scoreSource!=='score'.

findings.title: Vintage date gaps (7 missing days in 5 weeks) silently shorten N-day window coverage
findings.description: picks-history is missing 2026-05-12,05-16,05-18,05-27,06-03,06-09,06-11 — 7 gaps in a 5-week span. listVintages just globs whatever files exist; nothing detects or reports the gaps. For method-effectiveness the MIN_VINTAGES gate counts distinct dates present, so gaps reduce the count silently; for walk-forward each vintage is independent so gaps mainly reduce sample size without warning. Combined with near-daily cadence elsewhere, the irregular spacing also worsens the overlapping-window dependence (F-BT-005) non-uniformly.
findings.mechanism: No expected-cadence check; readdirSync filter+sort accepts any subset of dates. Missing vintages are invisible.
findings.reproducer: ls picks-history shows 2026-05-11 then 2026-05-13 (05-12 missing), 05-15 then 05-17, etc.
findings.impact: Reported vintageCount understates intended coverage; readers cannot tell whether a low count is by-design gating or a pipeline outage that dropped vintages. Erodes trust in n-based gates.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a coverage diagnostic (expected business days vs present vintages in the window) in walk-forward.json; warn when >X% of expected vintages are missing.

findings.title: Backtest scripts use TODAY's snapshot fundamentals against past prices (self-flagged)
findings.description: backtest-10-weeks.js and backtest-from-history.js both evaluate Runner.evaluateStock on the CURRENT snapshot and measure historical returns — textbook look-ahead bias (today's fundamentals were not known 10 weeks ago). Both now stamp _bias.lookAheadBias=true and name walk-forward-perf.js as the preferred alternative, which is good. Residual risk: both write to the SAME file backtest-10w-result.json with different schemas, so whichever ran last defines the artifact, and a stale committed copy may predate the _bias stamp.
findings.mechanism: evaluateStock(currentSnapshot) -> cohorts -> historical price return; the from-history variant additionally has the HORIZON_DAYS bug (F-BT-003).
findings.reproducer: Both files write './backtest-10w-result.json'; schemas differ (one has stocksTotal/passAvgReturn, the other alphaAvg/passCohort).
findings.impact: Look-ahead is acknowledged but the shared output path means consumers cannot tell which script produced the file; a committed pre-_bias artifact would be consumed as unbiased.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the two scripts distinct output filenames; ensure the _bias block is always present; consider deleting backtest-from-history.js (superseded and additionally buggy).

findings.title: Benchmark choice is availability-ordered (SPY>QQQ>IWM), not strategy-matched
findings.description: computeBenchmarkReturn picks the first available of [SPY,QQQ,IWM]. SPY (large-cap blend) is the alpha benchmark even for HYPERGROWTH and TURNAROUND modes whose universe is growth/small-cap — a style mismatch that systematically biases alpha (growth modes show positive alpha vs SPY in growth-up regimes regardless of skill). Worse, the chosen benchmark can differ across vintages purely by which series happens to be present that day, so the benchmark identity is not even held constant.
findings.mechanism: for t of [SPY,QQQ,IWM]: if present break. No mode-to-benchmark mapping; selection driven by data availability.
findings.reproducer: Read lines 276-284; first-present wins regardless of which mode is being scored.
findings.impact: alphaVsBenchmark conflates style/beta exposure with skill, and is not comparable across vintages if the resolved benchmark ticker changes. methodology-report presents this as the headline 'most honest' metric.
findings.suggested_fix: Map each mode to a style-appropriate benchmark (growth->QQQ/IWO, turnaround->IWM/value) and hold it fixed; record benchmarkTicker per vintage and refuse to aggregate across differing benchmarks.

findings.title: Transaction costs, spread, slippage, FX ignored across entire backtest stack
findings.description: returnPct is a raw close-to-close percentage. No commission, bid/ask spread, slippage, or FX conversion is applied anywhere in walk-forward, method-effectiveness, or the lookback scripts. Picks include non-USD tickers (e.g. 6160.HK in the 2026-05-08 vintage) whose Yahoo close is in local currency, so returns are correct in local terms but alpha vs a USD benchmark mixes currency moves into the comparison.
findings.mechanism: (p1-p0)/p0*100 with no cost model; cross-currency picks compared to USD SPY without FX normalization.
findings.impact: Reported alpha is gross and partly currency-driven for non-US picks; turnover-heavy modes overstate net edge. Low severity for a relative sanity-check tool but material if used to size positions.
findings.suggested_fix: Document gross-return assumption prominently; for cross-currency picks convert to USD before benchmark comparison, or restrict universe-median/benchmark alpha to same-currency cohorts.

findings.title: compute-picks-lookback: short-history stocks mislabeled by lookback year + duplicate fetches
findings.description: totalReturn requests period1=now-Nyears but uses hist[0]..hist[last] without checking that hist[0] is actually ~N years back. A stock that IPO'd 2 years ago returns its 2-year return under the 5y label (yf.historical clamps to available data). Additionally, processMode fetches each ticker's 1/3/5y return twice (once for the median block lines 70-80, again per-pick lines 99-107) — doubling API calls and rate-limit exposure.
findings.mechanism: first=hist[0], last=hist[last]; no assertion on hist[0].date vs past. Per-pick loop re-issues the same totalReturn calls already made for the median.
findings.reproducer: Read lines 49-55 (no date-span check) and 70-107 (same totalReturn(p.ticker,lb) issued in both loops).
findings.impact: Lookback medians blend genuine 5y returns with shorter spans labeled 5y, biasing the survivorship-already-warned sanity check further. Duplicate fetches roughly 2x runtime/quota.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or relabel a series whose first date is not within ~30d of the requested period1; compute per-pick returns once and reuse for the median.
